title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is a very faint pencil first draft of 'Lemme 1' and its 'Corollaire'. The next page (35) recopies and corrects it, so the reading below relies on p.35 and on the visible skeleton here: 'Lemme 1 soit [x,y]→ ...', 'Convention', 'f_xy(...) ... f_xy(...) + ... f_yx(...)', 'f_xy([..]×[..])', 'Corollaire ... x,y ∈ V^·· ...', 'Π V^··'.

Setting.
- V is a real vector space (or affine space) and V_C its complexification.
- Δ is a real line or hyperplane, with complexification Δ_C. V^{**} (written V^·· here) is apparently the complement of a configuration of such complexified real hyperplanes, or a space attached to Σ^*.
- φ_∞ is apparently an antiholomorphic involution, essentially complex conjugation, fixing the real points.
- For real points x, y there are two paths from x to y:
  - the straight real segment L_{y,x}(t) = t(x−y)+y (p.35 margin);
  - the half-circle l_{y,x}(t) = (x+y)/2 + e^{iπt}(x−y)/2, lying in the complex line through x and y.

Lemma. Consider the straight-line homotopy f_{x,y}(s,t) = (1−s)·φ_∞(l_{y,x}(t)) + s·l_{y,x}(t). For fixed t it joins the conjugate half-circle to the half-circle. If Δ does not meet the segment [x,y], the image of [0,1]² does not meet Δ_C.

Proof check. Write p = l(t). The points of the homotopy are z = Re p + i(2s−1)·Im p. Re p runs over the real segment [x,y], so a real affine equation λ of Δ cannot vanish at Re z. Hence z ∉ Δ_C.

Corollary. For x, y in V^{**} that are real (corresponding to distinct points of Σ^*), the square formed by l_{y,x}, the paths L_{x,φ_∞(x)} and L_{y,φ_∞(y)}, and φ_∞(l_{y,x}) commutes in the fundamental groupoid Π_1 V^{**}. Equivalently, φ_∞(l_{y,x}) is identified with a standard path. In words, complex conjugation acts trivially, or in a controlled way, on canonical paths between real base points lying in one chamber.

Purpose. This is a technical step toward describing complex conjugation (the 'real' element, cf. Gal(C/R) inside Gal(Q̄/Q)) acting on fundamental groupoids with real base points: chambers of real arrangements, real points of M_{0,n}. That is the setting of the Teichmüller groupoid / 'Teichmüller tower' programme in this file.
errors: The hypothesis as written on p.35, 'Δ ∩ {x,y} = ∅', is too weak if it means only the endpoints. If Δ meets the open segment ]x,y[, the midpoint level s = 1/2 of the homotopy is the real point Re l(t), which lies on Δ for some t. The correct hypothesis is Δ ∩ [x,y] = ∅, i.e. x and y lie in the same chamber. The present draft's text is illegible on this point.

ideas.what: Straight-line homotopy between the upper half-circle path and its complex conjugate, avoiding a complexified real hyperplane, when the real segment [x,y] avoids that hyperplane
ideas.modern_name: Paths between real points (chambers) in complements of complexified real arrangements; positive paths / Salvetti-type cell structure
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (1972, 'Les immeubles des groupes de tresses généralisés'); Salvetti (1987)

ideas.what: Action of complex conjugation φ_∞ on the fundamental groupoid with real base points: a commutative square in Π_1 V^{**}
ideas.modern_name: Complex conjugation acting on the fundamental groupoid with real (tangential) base points; the real element of Gal(Q̄/Q) acting on Teichmüller groupoids
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara, Drinfeld (1990, element of the GT group), Nakamura; Grothendieck's Esquisse (general idea)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses base points and Galois action in general terms; this specific lemma is not there

deep.surprise_reason: This is a faint preliminary draft of an elementary topological lemma (a straight-line homotopy) that is fully recopied on the next page. The mathematics is routine and well known.
